Tente dividir o numerador (ex: 310) por 2. O resultado dessa conta será o valor que vai sobre o 100.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: First identify the whole supply and the amount being compared with that whole in each row.
Place the amount being considered in the numerator and the original supply in the denominator.
For Part 2, determine how many people still want cookies after 283 people go elsewhere.
Subtract the people who go elsewhere from the original demand, then place that remaining amount over the supply of 200.
Ask whether the denominator must become smaller or larger when it changes from 200 to 100.
Choose the same operation for the numerator and denominator so the ratio remains equivalent.
The denominator changes from 200 to 100, so use an operation that reduces 200 by half.
Select multiplication in every numerator and denominator selector; the factor used afterward will be less than 1.
A scale factor tells how many times the original value is multiplied.
Find the factor by asking what number multiplied by 200 gives 100.
Because 100 is half of 200, the factor must represent one half.
Enter the decimal multiplier for one half in all six scale-factor fields.
Equivalent ratios change both parts by the same scale factor.
Multiply each original numerator by the factor entered in the previous step.
For Part 1, halve 310; for Part 2, first use the remaining demand after 283 people go elsewhere.
Calculate 200 times one half, 310 times one half, and 27 times one half, then enter those three results.
A ratio with denominator 100 can be read directly as a percentage.
Use each scaled numerator as the numerator over 100, then enter the same number as the percentage.
The three scaled numerators are found in the previous row of work; copy each one into both result fields for its row.
For each row, enter the scaled numerator first and then repeat that value in the percentage field.

exercicio.statement:
Adisa has a booth at the county fair. She baked 200 cookies, but supply does not meet demand.

Part 1) If 310 people each want to buy one of her cookies, what percentage of her supply is in demand?

Part 2) If 283 people go elsewhere, what percentage of her original supply is NOT in demand?

nodes.instruction: A ratio needs two related quantities in every row. Enter both the amount being compared and the original supply of 200.

nodes.description: Aluno acredita que multiplicar sempre aumenta o valor, ignorando que multiplicar por um número menor que 1 reduz o resultado
nodes.instruction: Division can also describe reducing the values, but this table uses multiplication by a factor less than 1. Select × so the later factor can be 0.5.

nodes.description: Aluno usa a diferença entre os números em vez da relação multiplicativa
nodes.instruction: You used the difference 200 − 100 instead of a multiplier. A scale factor must multiply the original value.

nodes.description: Aluno inverte o fator de escala (ex: usa 2 em vez de 0.5)
nodes.instruction: The factor 2 would make 200 become 400. To reduce 200 to 100, use a factor smaller than 1.
